234
CONFOCAL QUADRIO SURFACES.
[149.
The surface-integral for the corresponding element of the
surface $a+d a$ will be
$$+\frac{d V}{d \alpha} \frac{D_{1}^{2}}{c} d \beta d \gamma+\frac{d^{2} V}{d a^{2}} \frac{D_{1}^{2}}{c} d a d \beta d \gamma$$
since $D_{1}$ is independent of $a$. The surface-integral for the two
opposite faces of the element of volume will be the sum of these
quantities, or
$$\frac{d^{2} V}{d a^{2}} \frac{D_{1}^{2}}{c} d a d \beta d \gamma$$
Similarly the surface-integrals for the other two pairs of faces
will be
$$\frac{d^{2} V}{d \beta^{2}} \frac{D_{2}{ }^{2}}{c} d \alpha d \beta d \gamma \text { and } \frac{d^{2} V}{d \gamma^{2}} \frac{D_{3}{ }^{2}}{c} d \alpha d \beta d \gamma$$
These six faces enclose an element whose volume is
$$d s_{1} d s_{2} d s_{3}=\frac{D_{1}^{2} D_{2}^{2} D_{3}^{2}}{c^{3}} d a d \beta d \gamma$$
and if $\rho$ is the volume-density within that element, we find by
Art. 77 that the total surface-integral of the element, together
with the quantity of electricity within it multiplied by $4 \pi$, is
zero, or, dividing by $d a d \beta d \gamma$,
$$\frac{d^{2} V}{d a^{2}} D_{1}^{2}+\frac{d^{2} V}{d \beta^{2}} D_{2}^{2}+\frac{d^{2} V}{d \gamma^{2}} D_{3}^{2}+4 \pi \rho \frac{D_{1}^{2} D_{2}^{2} D_{3}^{2}}{c^{2}}=0$$
(11)
which is the form of Poisson's extension of Laplace's equation
referred to ellipsoidal coordinates.
If $\rho=0$ the fourth term vanishes, and the equation is equi-
valent to that of Laplace.
For the general discussion of this equation the reader is
referred to the work of Lamé already mentioned.
149.] To determine the quantities $a, \beta, \gamma$, we may put them in
the form of ordinary elliptic integrals by introducing the auxiliary
angles $\theta, \phi$, and $\psi$, where
$$\begin{aligned}
& \lambda_{1}=b \sin \theta \\
& \lambda_{2}=\sqrt{c^{2} \sin ^{2} \phi+b^{2} \cos ^{2} \phi} \\
& \lambda_{\mathrm{a}}=c \sec \psi
\end{aligned}$$
(12)
(13)
(14)
If we put $b=k c$, and $k^{2}+k^{\prime 2}=1$, we may call $k$ and $k^{\prime}$ the
two complementary moduli of the confocal system, and we find
$$a=\int_{0}^{\theta} \frac{d \theta}{\sqrt{1-k^{2} \sin ^{2} \theta}}$$
(15)
an elliptic integral of the first kind, which we may write ac-
cording to the usual notation $F(k, \theta)$.

since $D_{1}$ is independent of $a$. The surface-integral for the two
 opposite faces of the element of volume will be the sum of these
 quantities, or

$$\frac{d^{2} V}{d a^{2}} \frac{D_{1}^{2}}{c} d a d \beta d \gamma$$


Similarly the surface-integrals for the other two pairs of faces
 will be

$$\frac{d^{2} V}{d \beta^{2}} \frac{D_{2}{ }^{2}}{c} d \alpha d \beta d \gamma \text { and } \frac{d^{2} V}{d \gamma^{2}} \frac{D_{3}{ }^{2}}{c} d \alpha d \beta d \gamma$$


These six faces enclose an element whose volume is

$$d s_{1} d s_{2} d s_{3}=\frac{D_{1}^{2} D_{2}^{2} D_{3}^{2}}{c^{3}} d a d \beta d \gamma$$

and if $\rho$ is the volume-density within that element, we find by
 Art. 77 that the total surface-integral of the element, together
 with the quantity of electricity within it multiplied by $4 \pi$, is
 zero, or, dividing by $d a d \beta d \gamma$,

$$\begin{equation*}
\frac{d^{2} V}{d a^{2}} D_{1}^{2}+\frac{d^{2} V}{d \beta^{2}} D_{2}^{2}+\frac{d^{2} V}{d \gamma^{2}} D_{3}^{2}+4 \pi \rho \frac{D_{1}^{2} D_{2}^{2} D_{3}^{2}}{c^{2}}=0 \tag{11}
\end{equation*}$$

which is the form of Poisson's extension of Laplace's equation
 referred to ellipsoidal coordinates.


If $\rho=0$ the fourth term vanishes, and the equation is equi
valent to that of Laplace.


For the general discussion of this equation the reader is
 referred to the work of Lamé already mentioned.

149.] To determine the quantities $a, \beta, \gamma$, we may put them in
 the form of ordinary elliptic integrals by introducing the auxiliary
 angles $\theta, \phi$, and $\psi$, where

$$\begin{align*}
& \lambda_{1}=b \sin \theta  \tag{12}\\
& \lambda_{2}=\sqrt{c^{2} \sin ^{2} \phi+b^{2} \cos ^{2} \phi}  \tag{13}\\
& \lambda_{\mathrm{a}}=c \sec \psi \tag{14}
\end{align*}$$


If we put $b=k c$, and $k^{2}+k^{\prime 2}=1$, we may call $k$ and $k^{\prime}$ the
 two complementary moduli of the confocal system, and we find

$$\begin{equation*}
a=\int_{0}^{\theta} \frac{d \theta}{\sqrt{1-k^{2} \sin ^{2} \theta}} \tag{15}
\end{equation*}$$

an elliptic integral of the first kind, which we may write ac
cording to the usual notation $F(k, \theta)$.
